sentences.en: This week, Donald Trump returns to the White House, and he's promised, on day one, to begin carrying out the largest domestic deportation operation in American history.
sentences.zh: 本周，唐纳德·特朗普重返白宫，他承诺在上任第一天就开始执行美国历史上最大规模的国内驱逐行动。

sentences.en: Trump plans to mobilize federal and local law enforcement to remove millions of undocumented immigrants from the country.
sentences.zh: 特朗普计划动员联邦和地方执法部门，将数百万无证移民从国内驱逐出境。

sentences.en: But already, he's facing pushback from cities and states across the country that have declared themselves sanctuaries and say they won't cooperate.
sentences.zh: 但目前，他正面临来自全国各地宣布自己为“庇护城市”或“庇护州”的阻力，这些地方表示不会配合。

sentences.en: This is a fight we've had many times before.
sentences.zh: 这是一场我们以前经历过多次的斗争。

sentences.en: And back in 2017, during Trump's first term, we aired a two-part series exploring the origins of the sanctuary movement.
sentences.zh: 早在2017年，也就是特朗普的第一个任期内，我们曾播出过一个两部分的系列节目，探讨了“庇护运动”的起源。

sentences.en: We thought this would be a good week to revisit that story.
sentences.zh: 我们认为本周重温那个故事非常合适。

sentences.en: In July 1980, a group of Salvadoran migrants crossed the border from Mexico into Arizona.
sentences.zh: 1980年7月，一群萨尔瓦多移民越过墨西哥边境进入亚利桑那州。

sentences.en: They walked over an isolated mountain range and halfway across a wide desert valley.
sentences.zh: 他们翻过了一座孤立的山脉，走过了一片广阔沙漠山谷的一半路程。

sentences.en: There were more than two dozen of them, people who'd left behind lives and jobs to come to the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们有二十多人，都是抛下生活和工作来到美国的人。

sentences.en: They'd hired some guides to lead them on the journey.
sentences.zh: 他们雇了一些向导带路。

sentences.en: Reporting our story this week is Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 本周报道我们故事的是德莱尼·霍尔。

sentences.en: And those guides had brought them to a largely uninhabited part of the border.
sentences.zh: 那些向导把他们带到了边境上一片几乎无人居住的地区。

sentences.en: It was a vast, empty, and fatally hot stretch of the Sonoran Desert.
sentences.zh: 那是索诺兰沙漠中一片广阔、荒凉且酷热致命的地带。

sentences.en: The temperature the next day got up to around 112, 115 degrees out there.
sentences.zh: 第二天那里的气温高达112到115华氏度（约44到46摄氏度）。

sentences.en: He's a Presbyterian minister from Tucson, which is a couple of hours from where the migrants crossed.
sentences.zh: 他是图森市的一位长老会牧师，图森距离移民越境的地方只有几个小时的路程。

sentences.en: They were in the middle of the most desolate and deadly area of the desert.
sentences.zh: 他们当时正处于沙漠中最荒凉、最致命的区域中心。

sentences.en: And I think out of the group of 26, 12 of them died the first day out.
sentences.zh: 我认为在那26人中，有12人在出发的第一天就死了。

sentences.en: The survivors were eventually found, delirious and suffering from intense dehydration and heat stroke.
sentences.zh: 幸存者最终被发现时，神志不清，正遭受严重的脱水和中暑折磨。

sentences.en: Some of them had stripped off their clothes.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至脱光了衣服。

sentences.en: Border Patrol agents brought them to a hospital in Tucson, which is where Reverend John Fife met them.
sentences.zh: 边境巡逻队将他们送到了图森的一家医院，约翰·法伊夫牧师就是在那里见到他们的。

sentences.en: And they asked some of us who were pastors to provide some pastoral care for the survivors who were traumatized beyond understanding.
sentences.zh: 他们请求我们这些牧师为那些受到难以言喻创伤的幸存者提供一些牧灵关怀。

sentences.en: And they began to tell me why they'd fled El Salvador.
sentences.zh: 他们开始向我讲述为什么要逃离萨尔瓦多。

sentences.en: At that point, Reverend Fife had lived in Tucson for more than 10 years, leading a small congregation at a church called Southside Presbyterian.
sentences.zh: 当时，法伊夫牧师已经在图森生活了十多年，在一家名为“南区长老会”的教堂领导一个小会众。

sentences.en: He didn't know much about Central America or what was going on in countries like Nicaragua, Guatemala, and El Salvador around this time.
sentences.zh: 那时他对中美洲，或者当时尼加拉瓜、危地马拉和萨尔瓦多等国发生的事情知之甚少。

sentences.en: Not only ignorant, but I couldn't have put El Salvador on a map.
sentences.zh: 我不仅无知，甚至连萨尔瓦多在地图上的位置都找不到。

sentences.en: I knew it was somewhere between Mexico and Panama, but that was the extent of my knowledge.
sentences.zh: 我知道它在墨西哥和巴拿马之间，但这就是我知识的全部了。

sentences.en: So I had a lot to learn and a lot of catching up to do.
sentences.zh: 所以我有很多东西要学，有很多功课要补。

sentences.en: The people of El Salvador are caught in a web of terror, trapped between the military forces of the Irina government and the guerrilla forces of the FMLN.
sentences.zh: 萨尔瓦多人民陷入了一张恐怖之网，被伊里纳政府的军事力量和法拉本多·马蒂民族解放阵线（FMLN）的游击队夹在中间。

sentences.en: No one is safe in this civil war.
sentences.zh: 在这场内战中，没有人是安全的。

sentences.en: El Salvador's civil war had been decades in the making.
sentences.zh: 萨尔瓦多的内战酝酿了数十年。

sentences.en: Since the early 1900s, the country had been ruled by a series of oligarchs and corrupt military leaders.
sentences.zh: 自20世纪初以来，该国一直由一系列寡头和腐败的军事领导人统治。

sentences.en: They maintained control by repressing large segments of the rural population.
sentences.zh: 他们通过镇压农村人口的大部分来维持控制。

sentences.en: In the late 1970s and early 1980s, a number of left-wing guerrilla groups began to grow in power and influence.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代末和80年代初，一些左翼游击组织开始壮大，影响力不断提升。

sentences.en: The military responded by trying to crush this resistance.
sentences.zh: 军方则试图通过武力粉碎这种抵抗。

sentences.en: Death squads targeted union leaders, community organizers, and other people they suspected of sympathizing with the guerrillas.
sentences.zh: 死亡小队以工会领袖、社区组织者和其他被怀疑同情游击队的人为目标。
这其中也包括神职人员和修女。

sentences.en: Lots of civilians were caught in the middle of this violence.
sentences.zh: 许多平民被卷入了这场暴力冲突中。

sentences.en: Thousands of people were disappeared, murdered, or displaced.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人失踪、被杀或流离失所。

sentences.en: Today, the Salvadoran people continue to suffer as a persistent pattern of brutal human rights violations grips the nation.
sentences.zh: 今天，萨尔瓦多人民继续遭受苦难，因为一种持续的残酷侵犯人权模式正笼罩着这个国家。

sentences.en: And El Salvador wasn't the only country where this was happening.
sentences.zh: 而且萨尔瓦多并不是唯一发生这种情况的国家。

sentences.en: Similar conflicts were unfolding in Nicaragua and Guatemala, where authoritarian governments were facing pressure from left-wing rebels.
sentences.zh: 类似的冲突也在尼加拉瓜和危地马拉上演，那里的威权政府正面临来自左翼叛军的压力。

sentences.en: This is the history Reverend John Fyfe started to learn about when he met the Salvadoran migrants who'd nearly died in the desert near Tucson.
sentences.zh: 这就是约翰·法伊夫牧师在遇到那些在图森附近沙漠中差点丧命的萨尔瓦多移民时，开始了解到的历史。

sentences.en: Well, basically, they were telling me why they'd fled El Salvador, about threats from death squads, killings of members of their family or close friends, that sort of thing,
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本上，他们告诉我为什么要逃离萨尔瓦多，关于死亡小队的威胁，关于家人或密友被杀，诸如此类的事情，

sentences.en: and the reason why they'd had to flee.
sentences.zh: 以及他们为什么不得不逃离的原因。

sentences.en: He didn't know it then, but Reverend Fyfe was witnessing the beginning of something big.
sentences.zh: 他当时并不知道，法伊夫牧师正在见证一件大事的开端。

sentences.en: Hundreds of thousands of Central Americans were trying to get away from these dangerous and bloody civil wars.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的中美洲人正试图逃离这些危险而血腥的内战。

sentences.en: They were fleeing their countries, making their way through Mexico, and crossing into the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们逃离自己的国家，穿过墨西哥，进入美国。

sentences.en: So, a major migration of refugees occurred along this border during that 10-year period, beginning in 1980.
sentences.zh: 因此，从1980年开始的这十年间，边境沿线发生了大规模的难民迁移。

sentences.en: Reverend Fyfe's church sat less than 100 miles from the border, and it would be completely swept up in this crisis.
sentences.zh: 法伊夫牧师的教堂距离边境不到100英里，它将完全卷入这场危机之中。

sentences.en: Eventually, Fyfe and his congregants would give shelter to hundreds of Central Americans.
sentences.zh: 最终，法伊夫和他的会众为数百名中美洲人提供了庇护。

sentences.en: They'd be joined by a network of churches across the country, all opening their doors and giving migrants a safe place to stay.
sentences.zh: 他们得到了全国各地教会网络的支持，大家纷纷敞开大门，为移民提供安全的居所。

sentences.en: This would mark the beginning of a new and controversial social movement, based on the old religious concept of sanctuary.
sentences.zh: 这标志着一场基于古老宗教“庇护”概念的、新的且充满争议的社会运动的开始。

sentences.en: The idea that churches have a duty to shelter people fleeing persecution.
sentences.zh: 即教会负有庇护逃离迫害者的责任这一理念。

sentences.en: More than 6,000 people have signed up to provide sanctuary around the country.
sentences.zh: 全国已有超过6000人签署协议，承诺提供庇护。

sentences.en: The time today cracks down on so-called sanctuary cities.
sentences.zh: 今天，政府正在打击所谓的“庇护城市”。

sentences.en: The modern sanctuary movement in the U.S.
can trace its roots back to Reverend Fyfe.
sentences.zh: 可以追溯到法伊夫牧师。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to look at how it began and why it caused one of the biggest showdowns between church and state in recent memory.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨它是如何开始的，以及为什么它引发了近期记忆中教会与国家之间最大的对峙之一。

sentences.en: After that first encounter with the Salvadorans at the hospital,
sentences.zh: 在医院与萨尔瓦多人第一次接触后，

sentences.en: Reverend Fyfe began to see more and more Central Americans arriving in Tucson.
sentences.zh: 法伊夫牧师开始看到越来越多的中美洲人抵达图森。

sentences.en: Some of them would come to his church and ask for help.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人会来到他的教堂寻求帮助。

sentences.en: And at first, his inclination was to work within the rules of the immigration system.
sentences.zh: 起初，他的倾向是在移民系统的规则内行事。

sentences.en: I was pretty naive at that point.
And I went to the immigration office here in Tucson, met with the director and said,
sentences.zh: 我去了图森的移民局，见了局长并说，

sentences.en: we're seeing refugees who are fleeing for their lives.
sentences.zh: 我们看到有难民正在逃命。

sentences.en: What do we need to do to protect them?
sentences.zh: 我们需要做什么来保护他们？

sentences.en: And he said, well, we have good political asylum law in the books.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，我们有很好的政治庇护法律。

sentences.en: And if they're deserving of political asylum, if they're refugees, they'll get political asylum.
sentences.zh: 如果他们有资格获得政治庇护，如果他们是难民，他们就会得到政治庇护。

sentences.en: Asylum, you apply for if you are within the United States and have a well-founded fear of persecution.
sentences.zh: 如果你身在美国境内，并且有充分的理由担心受到迫害，你就可以申请庇护。

sentences.en: Since 1980, when Congress passed the Refugee Act,
sentences.zh: 自1980年国会通过《难民法》以来，

sentences.en: has asked people to meet a number of requirements in order to be granted political asylum.
sentences.zh: 一直要求人们满足一系列条件才能获得政治庇护。

sentences.en: They have to establish that they fear persecution in their home country,
sentences.zh: 他们必须证明他们担心在自己的国家受到迫害，

sentences.en: based on their race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or social group.
sentences.zh: 基于他们的种族、宗教、国籍、政治观点或社会群体。

sentences.en: They also have to convince immigration that their government is actually involved in their persecution,
sentences.zh: 他们还必须让移民局相信他们的政府确实参与了对他们的迫害，

sentences.en: or that it can't control the groups that are.
sentences.zh: 或者政府无法控制那些参与迫害的组织。

sentences.en: If someone shows up in the U.S.
and they can meet those requirements,
sentences.zh: 并且能够满足这些要求，

sentences.en: they're supposed to be able to stay.
But it's not always that simple.
sentences.zh: 但这并不总是那么简单。

sentences.en: Myers used to interview people seeking asylum,
sentences.zh: 迈尔斯过去常面试寻求庇护的人，

sentences.en: and she says it could be tough to establish a person's status.
sentences.zh: 她说确定一个人的身份可能很困难。

sentences.en: It relied heavily on a single individual's testimony about what they'd been through.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上依赖于个人对自己经历的陈述。

sentences.en: It depends on what they say and how they say it.
sentences.zh: 取决于他们说了什么以及怎么说的。

sentences.en: And if they have any backing.
sentences.zh: 以及他们是否有任何支持证据。

sentences.en: So basically, it was my decision,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这是我的决定，

sentences.en: based on my experience and what the person said.
sentences.zh: 基于我的经验和当事人的陈述。

sentences.en: there was very little physical evidence of this.
Despite the challenges of qualifying for asylum,
sentences.zh: 尽管获得庇护资格面临挑战，

sentences.en: Reverend Fife and his church raised some money
sentences.zh: 法伊夫牧师和他的教堂还是筹集了一些资金，

sentences.en: and organized legal assistance for the migrants.
sentences.zh: 并组织了为移民提供法律援助。
他们开始探访拘留中心，

sentences.en: and helping people fill out asylum applications.
sentences.zh: 并帮助人们填写庇护申请。

sentences.en: They arranged for lawyers to represent them in court.
sentences.zh: 他们安排律师在法庭上为他们辩护。

sentences.en: But it began to seem like even the people who met the requirements for asylum
sentences.zh: 但似乎即使是那些符合庇护要求的人，

sentences.en: Like, even in cases where there was physical evidence.
sentences.zh: 比如，即使在有物证的情况下也是如此。

sentences.en: I can remember taking in a guy who had been tortured in El Salvador.
sentences.zh: 我记得曾接收过一个在萨尔瓦多遭受过酷刑的人。

sentences.en: And we flew in an Amnesty International doctor who testified that,
sentences.zh: 我们请来了一位国际特赦组织的医生作证说，
是的，这个人确实遭受过酷刑。

sentences.en: I'm an expert on the physical effects of torture.
sentences.zh: 我是酷刑身体影响方面的专家。

sentences.en: And the immigration judge would order him deported the next day.
sentences.zh: 但移民法官第二天还是下令将他驱逐出境。

sentences.en: Reverend Fife began to wonder what was behind these decisions to deport.
sentences.zh: 法伊夫牧师开始怀疑这些驱逐决定背后的原因。

sentences.en: Central Americans hoping for asylum faced some significant hurdles.
sentences.zh: 希望获得庇护的中美洲人面临着一些重大障碍。

sentences.en: For one thing, just as they began turning up along the U.S.-Mexico border in 1980,
sentences.zh: 首先，就在1980年他们开始出现在美墨边境时，

sentences.en: tens of thousands of refugees from other places, like Cuba and Iran,
sentences.zh: 成千上万来自古巴和伊朗等其他地方的难民，

sentences.en: were also seeking refuge in the United States.
The government was overwhelmed with applications.
Most Central Americans had also, historically, come to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 历史上，大多数中美洲人来到美国也是为了工作，
政府更倾向于将他们视为经济移民。

sentences.en: The government was more inclined to see them as economic migrants.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，当时正值冷战时期。

sentences.en: And on top of that, there was the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 议长先生，各位尊敬的国会议员，

sentences.en: Mr. Speaker, distinguished members of the Congress,
sentences.zh: 各位尊贵的来宾，以及我的美国同胞们。

sentences.en: honored guests, and my fellow Americans.
sentences.zh: 1983年，罗纳德·里根总统在国会发表了一次特别电视讲话。

sentences.en: In 1983, President Ronald Reagan delivered a special televised speech before Congress.
sentences.zh: 在讲话中，他概述了对中美洲爆发内战的担忧。

sentences.en: In it, he outlined his concerns about the civil wars flaring up in Central America.
sentences.zh: 太多人认为中美洲只是墨西哥以南的一个地方，

sentences.en: Too many have thought of Central America as just that place way down below Mexico
sentences.zh: 不可能对我们的福祉构成威胁。

sentences.en: that can't possibly constitute a threat to our well-being.
sentences.zh: 这就是我要求召开这次会议的原因。

sentences.en: And that's why I've asked for this session.
sentences.zh: 中美洲的问题直接影响到我们自己人民的安全和福祉。

sentences.en: Central America's problems do directly affect the security and the well-being of our own people.

sentences.zh: 里根将中美洲视为冷战的重要前线，

sentences.en: Reagan saw Central America as an important front in the Cold War,
sentences.zh: 一个距离美国如此之近的地区，

sentences.en: a region so close to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 以至于我们的国家安全要求我们

sentences.en: that our national security required us
sentences.zh: 阻止共产主义运动在那里蔓延。

sentences.en: to stop communist movements from flourishing there.
sentences.zh: 尼加拉瓜距离迈阿密、圣安东尼奥、圣地亚哥和图森的距离，

sentences.en: Nicaragua is just as close to Miami, San Antonio, San Diego, and Tucson
sentences.zh: 和这些城市到我们今晚聚会的华盛顿的距离一样近。

sentences.en: as those cities are to Washington, where we're gathered tonight.
Just a few years earlier, in 1979,
sentences.zh: 尼加拉瓜确实发生了一场社会主义革命。

sentences.en: a socialist revolution actually did happen in Nicaragua.
sentences.zh: 桑地诺民族解放阵线推翻了一个美国支持的独裁政权，

sentences.en: The Sandinista National Liberation Front had ousted a U.S.-backed dictatorship,
sentences.zh: 该政权已经统治了这个国家几十年。

sentences.en: which had ruled the country for decades.
sentences.zh: 在这次演讲时，里根政府正在向反政府武装（Contras）提供援助，

sentences.en: At the time of this speech, the Reagan administration was sending aid to Contras,
sentences.zh: 以对抗新的社会主义桑地诺政府。

sentences.en: fighting the new socialist Sandinista government.
sentences.zh: 美国也在尽最大努力镇压萨尔瓦多和危地马拉类似的左翼运动，
这意味着支持那些在这些国家仍掌握权力的威权政府。

sentences.en: was also doing its best to suppress similar left-wing movements
sentences.zh: 总而言之，我要对你们说，今晚毫无疑问，
整个美洲的国家安全都系于中美洲。

sentences.en: which meant backing the authoritarian governments that still had a grip on power in those countries.
In summation, I say to you that tonight, there can be no question,
the national security of all the Americas is at stake in Central America.
So here's how this all connects back to Tucson and the deportations that Reverend Fyfe was seeing.
sentences.zh: 那么，这一切是如何与图森市以及法伊夫牧师所目睹的驱逐出境事件联系起来的呢？

sentences.en: government considered the governments of El Salvador and Guatemala
sentences.zh: 政府将萨尔瓦多和危地马拉的政府

sentences.en: to be political allies in the fight against communism,
sentences.zh: 视为反共斗争中的政治盟友，

sentences.en: it denied these governments were persecuting their own people.
sentences.zh: 所以它否认这些政府在迫害本国人民。

sentences.en: Under Reagan, almost all Salvadoran and Guatemalan border crossers
sentences.zh: 在里根执政期间，几乎所有萨尔瓦多和危地马拉的越境者

sentences.en: were classified not as political refugees, but as economic migrants.
sentences.zh: 都被归类为经济移民，而非政治难民。

sentences.en: That meant they didn't qualify for asylum.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们没有资格获得庇护。

sentences.en: Ruth Ann Myers, the former INS director in Arizona,
sentences.zh: 曾任亚利桑那州移民归化局局长的露丝·安·迈尔斯

sentences.en: says immigration officers followed policy set by the government,
